title: Unseen divider, sticky prompt, and jump-to-bottom
objective: Upgrade Swarm's scroll-away behavior so users get stable unseen-message boundaries, a sticky prior prompt header, and a jump-to-bottom pill during streaming work.
actions: Track the first scroll-away snapshot using message index and rendered content position.
Count unseen messages by user-visible assistant turns, not raw progress/tool-only events.
Keep the unseen divider stable as new messages stream or as earlier content is prepended/restored.
Render a sticky user prompt header when the current viewport is below the prompt that produced the visible output.
Add a clickable or key-triggered jump-to-bottom pill that restores sticky scroll and clears unseen state.

criteria: Progress, tool-only, and status-only events do not inflate the unseen count.
New assistant text while scrolled up produces a stable divider and bottom pill.
Jump-to-bottom restores sticky scroll without losing the divider prematurely during racey input batches.
Sticky prompt disappears when its original prompt is visible in the viewport.
Tests cover user scroll-away, assistant append, progress append, user submit, and jump-to-bottom.

non_goals: Do not add transcript search here; search is TASK-005.
Do not redesign message roles or runtime event schemas.
Do not make service-health panels visible by default.
findings: Unseen-message count now follows user-visible assistant message semantics: progress, tool/result, system, and thinking rows preserve scroll-away baseline but do not inflate the bottom pill count. Existing sticky prompt, divider, and jump-to-bottom reset behavior remains covered.
